pairs.difference: A: the stone wall and arch are a dull slate blue-grey with little chroma (0.057, below the real range). The one warm mass is the orange plank door, so the card reads as two flat families plus black iron. B: the cobalt door, cream wall, orange frame and green ivy with pink and yellow flowers all sit in the real chroma range, with clear hero and accent roles.
pairs.fix: Make the stone wall a clearer cool blue-lavender, with lighter lilac-blue faces and deeper violet-blue gaps between the stones. Add a little warm moss or a light rim on the arch so the background isn't grey.

pairs.difference: A: the witch hat is near-black charcoal with only a purple band, and its shadows fall to dead black-violet. The lens shows the hat as one dark mass on cyan, so the card has 1.6 hue families. Subject chroma (0.044) and shadow chroma kept (0.30) are both well below the real cards. B: the jacket is tan, orange and green, the shadows stay olive and rust, and its numbers sit inside the real range.
pairs.fix: Make the hat a deep plum-purple felt, not black. Lit faces should be a soft violet and shadow folds a rich indigo-purple. Add a small warm accent, such as a gold buckle on the band.

pairs.difference: A is a known real card from the anchor sheet: red bike, cool blue-grey car, peach sky. B: the dock planks, rowboat, rope and even the lily pads all collapse into one saturated orange-ochre family against flat cyan water. The wood has no muted brown, and the shadows inside the boat go the same orange-red.
pairs.fix: Paint the dock and boat as weathered brown wood with grey-tan tops. Make the shadows inside the boat cool brown-violet, the rope pale beige and the lily pads a true leaf green, so the wood is not all one orange.

pairs.difference: B: the pumpkin is pure saturated orange, at the top of the real subject-chroma range. The glowing face is pushed yellow, and the lens turns it into a pale cyan-grey patch. The weathered table is a dull grey-brown with a pale grain. A: the barrel is a warmer tan-orange with blue-grey steel hoops and a cool cyan sky, which separates hero and background the way the lessons' real cards do.
pairs.fix: Make the pumpkin a deeper red-orange, shading to a brownish-red in its grooves. Keep the face glow a warm amber, not a bright yellow. Paint the tabletop a clearer warm brown.

pairs.difference: B: the whole card is pulled warm (warm share 0.70, above the real 0.57). The porch wood, pumpkin, skin, boots and door frame are all orange-brown, and the lens shows the scene as one orange-tan mass with only a strip of sky as relief. A: the waterfall and sky are cool blue and teal against the pink pig and white sheep, so there are clear cool and warm roles.
pairs.fix: Cool the porch down: grey-blue painted floorboards and a cool blue-grey door. Keep orange only for the pumpkin.

pairs.difference: A: the floorboards fill the card with one saturated yellow-orange, so the card is pulled warm (0.79). The binocular shadows drop to near-black olive and charcoal, keeping too little chroma (0.425, below range). B: the roller coaster uses pure yellow, red and blue, but the sky and clouds give neutral rest, and its shadows stay rich blue.
pairs.fix: Draw the binocular shadows as deep forest green and the eyecups as dark navy, not black. Tone the floor down to a softer honey-tan with cooler brown gaps between the boards.

pairs.difference: A: a white ghost on lime-green rays is nearly two hues (1.5 families, warm share 0), and its shadow folds pick up green from the background. The subject's own chroma is far below the real cards (0.039). B: the jellyfish is a loud magenta and cyan on deep blue, but it holds three or four families, within range.
pairs.fix: Give the ghost a tinted local color: pale lavender-white sheet, soft blue-violet shadow folds and a faint pink blush. Change the background to a contrasting hue so the ghost has a clear identity.

pairs.difference: A: every balloon is pushed to a pure hue (red, orange, teal, purple), giving 5.5 hue families, above range. The sky behind them is a muted, low-chroma blue (0.107, below range). B: the bat is a muted plum-mauve with pink ears against a cleaner blue sky, a simple two-role palette within range.
pairs.fix: Use two or three balloon colors at most, for example red and yellow with one teal. Make the sky a brighter, cleaner blue behind them.

pairs.difference: B: the hot pink background bleeds into the wooden table, so the planks read pinkish-brown. The potion's green glow spreads onto the table as a lime cast, giving a pink against acid-green clash. A: the brown and gold chest on royal blue water with sand keeps believable local colors, and its shadows stay brown-violet.
pairs.fix: Paint the table a true warm brown with grey-brown shadows. Keep the green glow inside the bottle and use a softer magenta or violet background.

pairs.difference: B: the topiary, hedge and lawn are all one green family under a blue sky (warm share 0.046, below range; hue families at the bottom edge). Only the pale grey planter and a strip of path break it. A: the brown trunk, orange leaves and red turret roof set warm against cool green and blue.
pairs.fix: Add warm relief: a terracotta pot instead of grey stone, a warm sandy path, and a few flowers or warmer yellow-green highlights on the top tiers.

pairs.difference: B: the cauldron body and legs are flat black-grey, and their shadows drop to dead black (shadow chroma kept 0.35, far below the real 0.61). The lens shows the pot as a single dark mass against the purple floor, with only the acid-green brew and fire as color. A: the red cooler keeps rich red-crimson shadows and is set against blue sea and yellow sand.
pairs.fix: Make the cauldron a deep blue-violet iron, with lighter purple-grey on the lit side and rich indigo in the shadows. Let the green brew and the orange fire cast colored light on its rim and legs.

pairs.difference: B: a green background with a gold stand, a pure red ring and a purple swirl puts three loud complementaries on one card. The gold base is saturated yellow-orange with no muted brass. A: the blue vending machine on purple is cool-only (warm share 0.026, below range), but the multicolored cans give it relief and its shadows stay rich blue.
pairs.fix: Make the stand a muted antique brass with brown-olive shadows and replace the red ring with a dark wood ring. Shift the background to a deeper teal-green so the purple smoke is the one accent.

pattern: Generated cards push local colors toward one pure hue (orange wood, orange pumpkin, pure gold) or drop dark subjects to dead black, losing chroma in the shadows (witch hat, cauldron). They also spill the background hue or a glow onto props and the whole card (pink table, warm porch, green folds on the ghost). Real cards keep muted local browns and greys, cool or tinted shadows, and clear hero and background hue roles.
